title: Evaluating ElevenLabs Music v2 for Your Next Music Workflow
markdown:
If you are deciding whether to add an AI music tool to a creative workflow, begin with the specific controls and delivery path you need. ElevenLabs presents Music v2 as a generator with controls for genre, mood, instruments, and structure; it also describes section-level inpainting, genre transitions, multilingual generation, and long-form composition. [Source: ElevenLabs Music](https://elevenlabs.io/music)

A practical evaluation can start with one brief: define the intended genre, mood, instrumentation, song structure, and language, then create a draft and revise one selected section. This maps the test to the controls ElevenLabs describes, including regenerating a selected section without changing the rest of the song. [Source: ElevenLabs Music](https://elevenlabs.io/music) For product teams, ElevenLabs also states that Music v1 and Music v2 are available through its API for generation, audio reference, inpainting, and long-form composition. [Source: ElevenLabs Music](https://elevenlabs.io/music)

Licensing should be reviewed against the planned use case before publishing. ElevenLabs says self-serve plans permit online and offline commercial use except for film, TV, and Studio Games, while Enterprise plans permit all online and offline commercial use; its music page links to the model-specific terms for further detail. [Source: ElevenLabs Music](https://elevenlabs.io/music)

Cost is another useful checkpoint. The official pricing page lists a Free plan with 10,000 monthly credits and a Starter plan at $6 per month with 30,000 credits; it says credits are shared across products and estimates Eleven Music usage at 900 credits per minute. Prices exclude taxes, levies, and duties. [Source: ElevenLabs pricing](https://elevenlabs.io/pricing) Compare your expected music minutes with the available credit pool and verify the current plan details on the provider’s site.

Disclosure: This article contains an affiliate link.
